answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents form a peer-auditing web where each actor must stake collateral across an interaction horizon. If an adversary spawns fraudulent nodes to fabricate consensus, honest auditors run topological cut verifications to isolate the colluding cluster. Finding a sparse cut proves the cluster acts as a disconnected island of fake identities. Game-theoretic multi-agent auditing triggers stake slashing against the malicious partition, driving the attacker cost superlinear with network size while valid nodes flourish like an uncorrupted lotus.
